h14.rule: loss 0.25, 14-day Earth blackout: lost jobs (expired awards) sf_ll minus drop_retry, paired bootstrap CI excludes 0 below; and no reservation stuck past its timeout under sf_ll

link_shares.note: share of vehicle-steps with a radio path to the BASE mast (contact plan of the month, 60 s steps); mean over seeds

stuck_definition: Stuck reservations: a reservation whose holder has no path to the base at t_out + grace (60 s) and stays unheard; without the lost-link rule the base cannot confirm the release and must keep the silent vehicle's reserved volume blocked until it is heard (note 03 C7) - an UNCONFIRMED release, not a vehicle physically still in the segment (in the replay every vehicle leaves on schedule); with the rule the holder's behaviour is defined (it finishes or never enters a single-lane segment and stops at the next safe point), so the base releases it at its timeout: 0 stuck by construction (a property of the rule), and the hours that would otherwise have been blocked are reported. The count is large (98 %) because the single-lane segments lie on routes the BASE mast does not see: vehicles are linked 97.9 % of all time but only 54.5 % of driving time, and in seed 1 61 of the 91 reservations are on one segment of the CONSTR -> ISRU leg whose exit (route sample 190) is out of the mast's view (B-98a check). H14 (PREREG6): at loss 0.25 with the 14-day blackout, sf_ll loses fewer jobs than drop_retry (paired bootstrap CI of the difference excludes 0) and leaves no reservation stuck past its timeout.
outcome_definitions: Per kind: n messages; lost = expired undelivered inside the window (its lifetime ended); censored = still alive and undelivered at the window's end (fate unknown, not a loss; B-118 N4); lost_incl_censored = every undelivered message, the definition used before 13 Nov 2026. Since B-118 (N3) a bundle is never counted delivered after its lifetime, and a step gives it only the transmissions that fit; age of information is the exact time average of the sawtooth (N5; before, floored at 30 s).
lost_link_rule: Lost-link return (sf_ll): rule 'papers', as the papers state it, corrected after code review on 13 Nov 2026 (B-118 N6): a vehicle with no path to the base for T_hold = 600 s retraces at half speed the path it drove since the loss, so it is linked again at loss + 600 s + 2 x (its recorded driving time between the loss and the loss + 600 s). The replay uses the recorded trajectories, so the vehicle does not stop at the next safe point as note 03 C7 says: the retrace distance is an upper reading of the rule. Rows 'sf_ll_pre_review' replay the rule the code had before 13 Nov 2026 (T_hold + 2 x the driving time in the hour before the loss), on the same random stream as sf_ll.

h14_variants.note: H14 recomputed with lost = every undelivered award (the definition before 13 Nov 2026), and with the pre-review return rule; 'h14' above is the result

awards_and_jobs.note: B-117 (i), exploratory: one TASK_AWARD per vehicle of a job (run_e54.messages), so awards = jobs + the extra vehicles of team jobs

superseded_2026-11-13_b118.reason: B-118 step 2 (code review of 13 Nov 2026): the values published before the dtn.py fixes. N3: a store-and-forward bundle got a full set of transmissions in every step whatever time was left and its lifetime was checked only at the step's start, so grants could be delivered up to about 40 s late and counted delivered; an arrival on a step's last transmission was stamped at the next step. N4: bundles still alive at the window's end were counted lost (now 'censored'). N5: age of information was floored at dt/2 = 30 s. N6: the lost-link return used the driving time in the hour before the loss, which no text describes (now as the papers state it). C11: a relay's store limit was not checked on forwarding (no queue came near 64 MB, so no value moved by it). Kept as published, with the B-111 v0.2 block.

lrip_v02.task: B-111 (LEAD, 13 Nov): the E54 replay at LRIP v0.2 sizes
lrip_v02.note: Each seed's engine run and contact plan are made once and replayed with three size tables: v0.1 (the published values, as a reproduction check), v0.2 and v0.2 in Proximity-1 frames (+12 B per LRIP packet; the daily ledger bundle keeps its 10 kB). The replay sends TASK_AWARD, RESERVE_GRANT and TASK_STATE, whose v0.2 sizes equal v0.1 (v0.2 changed POSITION's spare bits and HELLO only), and in lunarsim/atc/dtn.py a size enters only the 64 MB per-node store limit, which no queue comes near; age of information uses STATUS beacons and no size. Unconfirmed-segment counts and hours come from the contact plan, not from sizes.
